title: Deep-fibrous against shallow-fibrous, on the one root axis that already exists
question: Do these read as two different root morphologies — a mat against a dive — or as the same chaotic tangle with a bit more of it?
context_md:
**No new mechanism, and no root code was written for this.** This is genome slot 5 (root tropism gain) at the two ends of what it can *actually* reach today: it multiplies the root's `upward_weight` by `1 ± 0.4`, so the whole reachable axis is 0.36 to 0.84 either side of the authored 0.6. Both panes are that, and nothing else — within-treatment genome noise on slot 5 is zeroed so the pane shows the treatment rather than eight coin flips.

Same scene, same seed, same frame (10,800), 8 founders, 4 shown. The grey band at the bottom is bedrock — how close a root gets to it is the question.

The method correction from `root-morphology-findings.md` applies and I have followed it: **single plants at zoom, never stand medians** — root cells span 90 to 1,435 within one stand, so a median is not a shape. The numbers under each pane are the *distribution*, not a summary.

What I already measured, so you do not have to judge it: the two treatments genuinely differ. One puts 79% of its root cells in the top two fifths of the profile; the other spreads 21/21/17/21/17 all the way to bedrock. What I cannot tell from a number is whether that difference **reads** — which is the thing two owner verdicts have already said no to for root work, on tuning-level changes.

This is the baseline for Arc B, so a "no" here is as useful as a yes: it would say the reachable axis is not enough and the thickening and dominance mechanisms have to land before root form is worth showing again.
